verses.before: for the ransom of their life is costly and forever beyond reach,
verses.after: the ransom for a life is too costly; one must give up the attempt forever—
verses.tsw_comparator: for the ransom of their life is costly and forever beyond reach,

verses.rationale: Connect purpose to the impossible ransom.
verses.before: that one should live on forever and never see the Pit.
verses.after: so that he might live on forever and never see the pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: that one should live on forever and never see the Pit.

verses.rationale: Retain shared mortality despite differences in wisdom.
verses.before: For one sees that the wise die; the fool and the senseless perish together and leave their wealth to others.
verses.after: Anyone can see that the wise die; fools and the senseless perish together and leave their wealth to others.
verses.tsw_comparator: For one sees that the wise die; the fool and the senseless perish together and leave their wealth to others.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned inward thought rather than silently changing to graves.
verses.before: Their graves are their homes forever, their dwellings from generation to generation, though they called lands by their own names.
verses.after: Their inward thought is that their houses will last forever, their dwellings through every generation; they name lands after themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their graves are their homes forever, their dwellings from generation to generation, though they called lands by their own names.

verses.rationale: Keep the first refrain’s endure verb distinct from verse 20.
verses.before: A human being in honor does not remain; one is like the beasts that perish.
verses.after: Human beings in splendor do not endure; they are like animals that perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: A human being in honor does not remain; one is like the beasts that perish.

verses.rationale: Preserve ambiguous followers’ approval and misplaced confidence.
verses.before: This is the way of people who are foolish, and after them come people who approve their words. Selah.
verses.after: This is the way of those with foolish confidence, and of those after them who approve their words. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the way of those who are foolish, and after them come those who approve their words. Selah.

verses.rationale: Follow read form and retain difficult final relation in a note.
verses.before: Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol; death will shepherd them. The upright will rule over them in the morning, and their form will waste away in Sheol, far from their lofty dwelling.
verses.after: Like sheep they are destined for Sheol; Death will shepherd them. The upright will rule over them at morning. Their form will waste away in Sheol, far from their dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol; death will shepherd them. The upright will rule over them in the morning, and their form will waste away in Sheol, far from their lofty dwelling.

verses.rationale: Keep personal hope without specifying timing or mechanism.
verses.before: Yet God will ransom my life from the hand of Sheol, for God will receive me. Selah.
verses.after: But God will ransom my life from Sheol’s hand, for he will take me. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God will ransom my life from the hand of Sheol, for God will receive me. Selah.

verses.rationale: Preserve warning against fear of wealth.
verses.before: Do not fear when someone becomes rich, when the glory of the house increases.
verses.after: Do not fear when someone grows rich, when the splendor of their house increases.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not fear when someone becomes rich, when the glory of the house increases.

verses.rationale: Keep descent and stripped possessions.
verses.before: For at death one will carry nothing away; one’s glory will not descend after them.
verses.after: At death they take none of it; their splendor does not descend after them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For at death one will carry nothing away; one’s glory will not descend after them.

verses.rationale: Retain aside’s shift to second person.
verses.before: Though while living one blesses one’s own life— and people praise you when you do well for yourself—
verses.after: Though they congratulate themselves while alive— and people praise you when you do well for yourself—
verses.tsw_comparator: Though while living one blesses one’s own life— and people praise you when you do well for yourself—

verses.rationale: Preserve final darkness in the poem’s own voice.
verses.before: one will go to the generation of one’s ancestors, who will never again see light.
verses.after: they will go to the generation of their ancestors, who will never see light again.
verses.tsw_comparator: one will go to the generation of one’s ancestors, who will never again see light.

verses.rationale: Keep changed refrain wording and wisdom emphasis.
verses.before: A human being in honor, yet without understanding, is like the beasts that perish.
verses.after: Human beings in splendor, without understanding, are like animals that perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: A human being in honor, yet without understanding, is like the beasts that perish.

verses.rationale: Preserve Asaph title and El, Elohim, YHWH in source order, followed by the summons spanning sunrise to sunset.
verses.before: The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
verses.after: A psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from the sun’s rising to its setting.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.

verses.rationale: Keep explicit beauty and divine appearance.
verses.before: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth.
verses.after: From Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth.

verses.rationale: Retain terrifying arrival and silence broken.
verses.before: Our God comes; he does not keep silence; before him is a devouring fire, and around him a mighty storm.
verses.after: Our God comes and will not stay silent. Fire devours before him; a fierce storm rages around him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our God comes; he does not keep silence; before him is a devouring fire, and around him a mighty storm.

verses.rationale: Keep cosmic witnesses and own people as defendants.
verses.before: He calls to the heavens above and to the earth, that he may judge his people:
verses.after: He summons heaven above and the earth to judge his people:
verses.tsw_comparator: He calls to the heavens above and to the earth, that he may judge his people:

verses.rationale: Preserve covenant-making ritual and divine summons.
verses.before: “Gather to me my faithful ones, who made a covenant with me by sacrifice!”
verses.after: “Gather my faithful ones to me, those who made my covenant by sacrifice.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Gather to me my faithful ones, who made a covenant with me by sacrifice!”

verses.rationale: Keep heavens as witness and judge’s identity.
verses.before: The heavens declare his righteousness, for God himself is judge.
verses.after: The heavens declare his righteousness, for God himself is judge. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heavens declare his righteousness, for God himself is judge.

verses.rationale: Mark renewed divine speech and covenantal address.
verses.before: “Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God.
verses.after: “Hear, my people, and I will speak. Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God.

verses.rationale: Keep precise denial rather than dismissing all sacrifice.
verses.before: Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you; your burnt offerings are continually before me.
verses.after: I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you; your burnt offerings are continually before me.

verses.rationale: Express refusal in context of divine ownership.
verses.before: I will not take a bull from your house, or goats from your folds,
verses.after: I need no bull from your house or male goats from your pens,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not take a bull from your house, or goats from your folds,

verses.rationale: Keep comprehensive ownership and stated number.
verses.before: for every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills.
verses.after: for every forest animal is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills.
verses.tsw_comparator: for every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills.

verses.rationale: Retain knowledge and ownership of nonhuman life.
verses.before: I know all the birds of the mountains, and all that moves in the field is mine.
verses.after: I know every bird of the mountains; the creatures of the fields are mine.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know all the birds of the mountains, and all that moves in the field is mine.

verses.rationale: Keep the hypothetical and ironic independence.
verses.before: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are mine.
verses.after: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and all it holds belong to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are mine.

verses.rationale: Preserve rhetorical challenge to feeding God.
verses.before: Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
verses.after: Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?

verses.rationale: Keep thanksgiving’s possible sacrificial sense and vowed obligations.
verses.before: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High,
verses.after: Offer thanksgiving as your sacrifice to God; fulfill your vows to the Most High.
verses.tsw_comparator: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High,

verses.rationale: Close first speech with relational response.
verses.before: and call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.”
verses.after: Call on me on a day of distress. I will rescue you, and you will honor me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me.”

verses.rationale: Keep new audience and challenge to empty recitation.
verses.before: But to the wicked God says: “What right have you to recite my statutes or take my covenant on your lips,
verses.after: But to the wicked God says, “What right have you to recite my statutes and take my covenant on your lips,
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the wicked God says: “What right have you to recite my statutes or take my covenant on your lips,

verses.rationale: Retain active rejection image.
verses.before: for you hate instruction and cast my words behind you?
verses.after: when you hate correction and throw my words behind you?
verses.tsw_comparator: for you hate instruction and cast my words behind you?

verses.rationale: Read ratzah as pleased approval and participation with a thief; retain separate company with adulterers.
verses.before: If you see a thief, you are pleased with him, and you keep company with adulterers.
verses.after: When you see a thief, you are pleased to join him; you throw in your lot with adulterers.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you see a thief, you are pleased with him, and you keep company with adulterers.

verses.rationale: Keep unrestricted speech and crafting deceit.
verses.before: You give your mouth free rein for evil, and your tongue frames deceit.
verses.after: You let your mouth loose for evil; your tongue weaves deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: You give your mouth free rein for evil, and your tongue frames deceit.

verses.rationale: Retain intensified kinship betrayal.
verses.before: You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.
verses.after: You sit and speak against your brother, slandering your own mother’s son.
verses.tsw_comparator: You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.

verses.rationale: Preserve mistaken inference from silence and confrontation.
verses.before: These things you have done, and I have been silent; you thought that I was one like yourself. But now I rebuke you and set them in order before your eyes.
verses.after: You did these things, and I stayed silent. You thought I was just like you. But I will rebuke you and lay it all before your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: These things you have done, and I have been silent; you thought that I was one like yourself. But now I rebuke you and set them in order before your eyes.

verses.rationale: Keep violent warning and absence of rescuer.
verses.before: “Mark this, then, you who forget God, lest I tear you apart, and there be none to deliver!
verses.after: Understand this, you who forget God, or I will tear you apart, with no one to rescue you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Mark this, then, you who forget God, lest I tear you apart, and there be none to deliver!

verses.rationale: Supply rightly from ethical context while noting compressed final clause.
verses.before: The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies me; to one who orders his way rightly I will show the salvation of God.”
verses.after: The one who offers thanksgiving honors me. To the one who orders their way rightly I will show God’s salvation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies me; to one who orders his way rightly I will show the salvation of God.”

verses.rationale: Bind both title records and opening prayer, preserving the sexual euphemism with a note.
verses.before: Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love. According to your abundant compassion, blot out my transgressions.
verses.after: For the music leader. A psalm of David, when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba. Be gracious to me, God, according to your faithful love; in your great compassion wipe away my rebellions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love. According to your abundant compassion, blot out my transgressions.

verses.rationale: Follow read imperative and retain washing/purification.
verses.before: Wash me thoroughly from my guilt, and cleanse me from my sin.
verses.after: Wash me thoroughly from my wrongdoing; cleanse me from my sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wash me thoroughly from my guilt, and cleanse me from my sin.

verses.rationale: Keep acknowledged responsibility and constant awareness.
verses.before: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
verses.after: I know my rebellions; my sin is always before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic alone without using it to deny human victims.
verses.before: Against you, you alone, have I sinned, and done what is evil in your sight, so that you are justified in your words and blameless in your judgment.
verses.after: Against you, you alone, I have sinned and done what is evil in your sight, so you are right when you speak and clear when you judge.
verses.tsw_comparator: Against you, you alone, have I sinned, and done what is evil in your sight, so that you are justified in your words and blameless in your judgment.

verses.rationale: Keep birth-to-conception imagery without assigning a specific maternal offense.
verses.before: Indeed, I was born into brokenness, and in sin my mother conceived me.
verses.after: I was brought forth in wrongdoing; in sin my mother conceived me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, I was born into brokenness, and in sin my mother conceived me.

verses.rationale: Retain obscure interior imagery with a concise note.
verses.before: Yet you desire truth in the inward being; you teach me wisdom in the hidden place.
verses.after: You desire truth in the inward parts; in the hidden place you teach me wisdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you desire truth in the inward being; you teach me wisdom in the hidden place.

verses.rationale: Keep ritual plant and cleansing comparison.
verses.before: Purge me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
verses.after: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

verses.rationale: Retain divine crushing and bodily restoration.
verses.before: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you have crushed rejoice.
verses.after: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you crushed rejoice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you have crushed rejoice.

verses.rationale: Preserve face turned from guilt rather than from the person.
verses.before: Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all my guilt.
verses.after: Hide your face from my sins; wipe away all my wrongdoings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all my guilt.

verses.rationale: Keep creation and renewal as paired requests.
verses.before: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
verses.after: Create a clean heart in me, God; renew a steadfast spirit within me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

verses.rationale: Retain holy spirit language without adding a later doctrinal definition.
verses.before: Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your holy spirit from me.
verses.after: Do not throw me out of your presence or take your holy spirit from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your holy spirit from me.

verses.rationale: Keep restoration of joy and willing disposition’s uncertain agency.
verses.before: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
verses.after: Restore to me the joy of your salvation; sustain me with a willing spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserve future instruction arising from restoration.
verses.before: Then I will teach transgressors your ways, and people who turn aside will return to you.
verses.after: Then I will teach rebels your ways, and sinners will return to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I will teach transgressors your ways, and those who turn aside will return to you.

verses.rationale: Keep bloodshed responsibility and promised praise.
verses.before: Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, O God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness.
verses.after: Rescue me from bloodguilt, God, the God who saves me; my tongue will sing of your righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, O God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness.

verses.rationale: Retain God enabling the speech.
verses.before: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
verses.after: Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will announce your praise.
verses.tsw_comparator: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.

verses.rationale: Keep the speaker’s hypothetical offering and divine refusal.
verses.before: For you do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it; you take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
verses.after: You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it; you take no pleasure in a burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it; you take no pleasure in burnt offerings.

verses.rationale: Preserve plural sacrifices and repeated brokenness.
verses.before: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, O God, you will not despise.
verses.after: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, God, you will not despise.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, O God, you will not despise.

verses.rationale: Keep communal turn without resolving compositional history.
verses.before: Do good to Zion in your good pleasure; rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.after: In your favor do good to Zion; rebuild Jerusalem’s walls.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do good to Zion in your good pleasure; rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain righteous sacrifices, burnt offerings and whole offerings without collapsing the paired terms; preserve final bulls and altar.
verses.before: Then you will delight in right sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole offerings; then bulls will be offered on your altar.
verses.after: Then you will delight in righteous sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole offerings; then bulls will be offered on your altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will delight in right sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole offerings; then bulls will be offered on your altar.

verses.rationale: Retain historical title and abrupt contrast with divine loyalty.
verses.before: Why do you boast of evil, mighty man? The steadfast love of God endures all the day.
verses.after: For the music leader. A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, “David has come to Ahimelech’s house.” Why boast of evil, you mighty man? God’s faithful love lasts all day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you boast of evil, mighty man? The steadfast love of God endures all the day.

verses.rationale: Keep tongue as destructive agent and sharp tool.
verses.before: Your tongue plots destruction, like a sharp razor, you worker of deceit.
verses.after: Your tongue plots ruin, like a sharpened razor, working deceit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your tongue plots destruction, like a sharp razor, you worker of deceit.

verses.rationale: Preserve comparative loves and ethical speech.
verses.before: You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking righteousness. Selah
verses.after: You love evil more than good, lies more than speaking rightly. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking righteousness. Selah

verses.rationale: Keep consuming speech and direct address to tongue.
verses.before: You love all words that devour, O deceitful tongue.
verses.after: You love every devouring word, you deceitful tongue!
verses.tsw_comparator: You love all words that devour, O deceitful tongue.

verses.rationale: Retain escalating destructive actions and uprooting.
verses.before: Yet God will break you down forever; he will snatch and tear you from your tent, he will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
verses.after: But God will tear you down forever; he will seize you, pull you from your tent, and uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God will break you down forever; he will snatch and tear you from your tent, he will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah

verses.rationale: Keep both fear and laughter without softening.
verses.before: The righteous will see and fear; they will laugh at him, saying,
verses.after: The righteous will see and fear; they will laugh at him:
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous shall see and fear; they shall laugh at him, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserve wrong refuge and difficult final source of strength.
verses.before: "See the man who would not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his riches and strengthened himself in his destruction."
verses.after: “Here is the man who would not make God his stronghold. He trusted in his great wealth and made himself strong through destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: "See the man who would not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his riches and strengthened himself in his destruction."

verses.rationale: Keep living tree contrast to uprooted enemy.
verses.before: Yet I am like a green olive tree in the house of God. I trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.
verses.after: But I am like a flourishing olive tree in God’s house; I trust in God’s faithful love forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God. I trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.

verses.rationale: Retain unusual waiting for name and communal setting.
verses.before: I will thank you forever, because you have done it. I will wait for your name, for it is good, in the presence of your faithful ones.
verses.after: I will thank you forever because you have acted. I will wait for your name, for it is good, in the presence of your faithful ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will thank you forever, because you have done it. I will wait for your name, for it is good, in the presence of your faithful ones.

verses.rationale: Keep title and this Psalm’s wrongdoing term distinct from Psalm 14.
verses.before: The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt and commit abominable injustice; there is none who does good.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to Mahalath. A maskil of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt and do abhorrent wrong; no one does good.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt and commit abominable injustice; there is none who does good.

verses.rationale: Retain God designation rather than harmonizing LORD from Psalm 14.
verses.before: God looked down from heaven upon the children of humanity to see if there is anyone who acts wisely, any who seek after God.
verses.after: God looks down from heaven on humanity to see whether anyone understands, whether anyone seeks God.
verses.tsw_comparator: God looked down from heaven upon the children of humanity to see if there is anyone who acts wisely, any who seek after God.

verses.rationale: Keep comprehensive repeated indictment.
verses.before: All have turned aside; together they have become corrupt. There is none who does good, not even one.
verses.after: All have turned away; together they have become corrupt. No one does good, not even one.
verses.tsw_comparator: All have turned aside; together they have become corrupt. There is none who does good, not even one.

verses.rationale: Retain unmarked my people voice and eating image.
verses.before: Do they not know, all evildoers, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call upon God?
verses.after: Do these evildoers know nothing, devouring my people as they eat bread, never calling on God?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do they not know, all evildoers, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call upon God?

verses.rationale: Preserve this Psalm’s distinct expanded judgment and second-person address.
verses.before: There they were in great fear where no fear was. For God scattered the bones of people who encamped against you; you put them to shame, for God rejected them.
verses.after: There they trembled with terror where there was no cause for terror. God scattered the bones of those camped against you; you put them to shame, for God rejected them.
verses.tsw_comparator: There they were in great fear where no fear was. For God scattered the bones of those who encamped against you; you put them to shame, for God rejected them.

verses.rationale: Keep communal longing and God rather than LORD.
verses.before: Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of his people, Jacob will rejoice; Israel will be glad.
verses.after: If only Israel’s salvation would come from Zion! When God restores his people’s fortunes, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of his people, Jacob will rejoice; Israel will be glad.

verses.rationale: Bind both title records and preserve specific informants.
verses.before: O God, by your name save me, and by your might vindicate me.
verses.after: For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Is not David hiding among us?” God, save me by your name; vindicate me by your power.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, by your name save me, and by your might vindicate me.

verses.rationale: Keep doubled appeal to hearing.
verses.before: O God, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth.
verses.after: God, hear my prayer; listen to the words of my mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth.

verses.rationale: Retain pinned strangers rather than substituting arrogant people.
verses.before: For strangers rise against me, and ruthless men seek my life. They have not set God before them. Selah
verses.after: Strangers have risen against me; ruthless men seek my life. They do not keep God before them. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: For strangers rise against me, and ruthless men seek my life. They have not set God before them. Selah

verses.rationale: Keep the unusual among construction without excluding divine primacy.
verses.before: Look, God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my life.
verses.after: Look, God is my helper; the Lord is among those who sustain my life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my life.

verses.rationale: Follow read causative and preserve sharp turn into direct destructive appeal.
verses.before: He will repay the evil to my foes; in your faithfulness, destroy them.
verses.after: He will turn evil back on those watching for my fall. In your faithfulness, destroy them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will repay the evil to my foes; in your faithfulness, destroy them.

verses.rationale: Keep voluntary offering and good name.
verses.before: With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to you; I will praise your name, O Lord, for it is good.
verses.after: I will freely offer you a sacrifice; I will thank your name, LORD, for it is good.
verses.tsw_comparator: With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to you; I will praise your name, O Lord, for it is good.

verses.rationale: Do not add triumph or desire absent from the final clause.
verses.before: For he has delivered me from every trouble, and my eye has looked in triumph on my enemies.
verses.after: He has rescued me from every distress; my eyes have looked upon my enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he has delivered me from every trouble, and my eye has looked in triumph on my enemies.

verses.rationale: Bind separate title with opening; keep plea against divine withdrawal.
verses.before: Give ear, O God, to my prayer, and do not hide yourself from my supplication.
verses.after: For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David. God, listen to my prayer; do not turn away from my plea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear, O God, to my prayer, and do not hide yourself from my supplication.

verses.rationale: Let complaint run into the cause in verse 3; arid expresses restless distress.
verses.before: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint and moan,
verses.after: Pay attention to me and answer. I am restless in my complaint, moaning
verses.tsw_comparator: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint and moan,

verses.rationale: Keep hostile speech and pressure, plural turn and anger rather than adding physical blows.
verses.before: because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked. For they bring down trouble on me, and in anger they bear a grudge against me.
verses.after: at the enemy’s voice, under the wicked man’s pressure. They heap trouble on me and pursue me in anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked. For they bring down trouble on me, and in anger they bear a grudge against me.

verses.rationale: Retain embodied writhing and death terrors.
verses.before: My heart is in anguish within me, and the terrors of death have fallen upon me.
verses.after: My heart writhes inside me; the terrors of death have fallen on me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My heart is in anguish within me, and the terrors of death have fallen upon me.

verses.rationale: Keep three cumulative fear expressions and covering image.
verses.before: Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror envelopes me.
verses.after: Fear and trembling come over me; horror covers me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror envelopes me.

verses.rationale: Dove wish is escape and rest without adding heaven.
verses.before: I say, "Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and be at rest;
verses.after: I said, “If only I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and settle somewhere.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I say, "Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and be at rest;

verses.rationale: Preserve wilderness lodging and pause within speech.
verses.before: look, I would wander far away; I would lodge in the wilderness. Selah
verses.after: I would wander far away and spend the night in the wilderness. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: behold, I would wander far away; I would lodge in the wilderness. Selah

verses.rationale: Close escape wish at storm; refuge motif remains concrete.
verses.before: I would hurry to find a shelter from the raging wind and tempest."
verses.after: I would hurry to find shelter from the rushing wind and storm.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I would hurry to find a shelter from the raging wind and tempest."

verses.rationale: Keep destructive imperative and divided tongues rather than reducing to confusion alone.
verses.before: Confuse, O Lord, divide their tongues, for I see violence and strife in the city.
verses.after: Swallow them up, Lord; divide their tongues! I see violence and conflict in the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Confuse, O Lord, divide their tongues, for I see violence and strife in the city.

verses.rationale: Allow violence and conflict personified as circling without identifying invented guards.
verses.before: Day and night they go around its walls, and iniquity and trouble are within it.
verses.after: Day and night they circle it on its walls; trouble and misery are inside it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Day and night they go around its walls, and iniquity and trouble are within it.

verses.rationale: Retain civic public square and persistence.
verses.before: Ruin is in its midst; oppression and deceit do not depart from its square.
verses.after: Destruction is within it; oppression and deceit never leave its square.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ruin is in its midst; oppression and deceit do not depart from its square.

verses.rationale: Unfold the two negative counterfactual clauses naturally before betrayal disclosure.
verses.before: For not an enemy insults me—then I could bear it. It is not one who hates me—who has raised himself against me; then I could hide from him.
verses.after: If an enemy were insulting me, I could bear it. If someone who hated me rose against me, I could hide from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For not an enemy insults me—then I could bear it. It is not one who hates me—who has raised himself against me; then I could hide from him.

verses.rationale: Specific male friend and rank retained, no invented identity.
verses.before: But you—a person of my equal, my companion and familiar friend.
verses.after: But it is you—a man my equal, my companion, my close friend.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you—a person of my equal, my companion and familiar friend.

verses.rationale: Keep intimate counsel contrasted with public shared worship.
verses.before: We used to take sweet counsel together; within God's house we walked in the throng.
verses.after: We shared the sweetness of private counsel and walked with the crowd in God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: We used to take sweet counsel together; within God's house we walked in the throng.

verses.rationale: Follow read two-word death clause and retain living descent and imprecation.
verses.before: Let death seize them; let them go down to Sheol alive. For evil is in their homes and within them.
verses.after: Let death take them by surprise; let them go down alive to Sheol! Evil lives in their homes and within them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let death seize them; let them go down to Sheol alive. For evil is in their homes and within them.

verses.rationale: Contrast first person with enemies, distinct divine names.
verses.before: Yet I call to God, and the Lord will save me.
verses.after: As for me, I call to God, and the LORD will save me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I call to God, and the Lord will save me.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three times and lament rather than substituting calm prayer.
verses.before: Evening and morning and at noon, I utter my complaint and moan, and he hears my voice.
verses.after: Evening, morning, and noon, I complain and moan; he hears my voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Evening and morning and at noon, I utter my complaint and moan, and he hears my voice.

verses.rationale: Render beshalom safety; with me can mean on my side or engaged against me, note choice.
verses.before: He redeems my soul in safety from the battle against me, for many are against me.
verses.after: He has ransomed me safely from the battle against me, though there were many opposing me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He redeems my soul in safety from the battle against me, for many are against me.

verses.rationale: Keep ancient enthronement and difficult no-changes clause, note alternatives.
verses.before: God will hear and answer them— he who is enthroned from of old—Selah because they do not change and do not fear God.
verses.after: God will hear and humble them— the one enthroned from long ago. Selah. They do not change, and they do not fear God.
verses.tsw_comparator: God will hear and answer them— he who is enthroned from of old—Selah because they do not change and do not fear God.

verses.rationale: Abrupt singular betrayer retained without adding name.
verses.before: My companion stretched out his hand against his friends; he has violated his covenant.
verses.after: He reaches out against those at peace with him; he has profaned his covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: My companion stretched out his hand against his friends; he has violated his covenant.

verses.rationale: Preserve butter/oil and war/sword paired contrasts.
verses.before: His speech was smooth as butter, yet war was in his heart. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.
verses.after: His mouth is smoother than butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, but they are drawn swords.
verses.tsw_comparator: His speech was smooth as butter, yet war was in his heart. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.

verses.rationale: Keep casting and sustaining, indefinite burden rather than invented problem list.
verses.before: Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you. He will never permit the righteous to be moved.
verses.after: Throw your burden onto the LORD; he will sustain you. He will never let the righteous be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you. He will never permit the righteous to be moved.

verses.rationale: Keep half-days claim, bloodshed and final personal trust.
verses.before: But you, O God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction. Men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days. Yet I will trust in you.
verses.after: But you, God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction. Men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. As for me, I will trust you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, O God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction. Men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in you.

verses.rationale: Title tune rendering tentative in note; preserve Philistines Gath and continuous oppression.
verses.before: Be gracious to me, O God, for people trample on me; all day long an attacker oppresses me.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to “The Silent Dove Far Away.” Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be gracious to me, God, for people trample me; all day an attacker presses me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be gracious to me, O God, for people trample on me; all day long an attacker oppresses me.

verses.rationale: Marom literally height, arrogance chosen over Most High address with note.
verses.before: My enemies trample upon me all day long, for many are fighting against me proudly.
verses.after: Those watching for my fall trample me all day; many fight against me arrogantly.
verses.tsw_comparator: My enemies trample upon me all day long, for many are fighting against me proudly.

verses.rationale: Fear and trust coexist, not denial of fear.
verses.before: When I am afraid, I will trust in you.
verses.after: On the day I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I am afraid, I will trust in you.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated in God and flesh contrasted with human in verse 11.
verses.before: In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
verses.after: In God, whose word I praise— in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
verses.tsw_comparator: In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?

verses.rationale: Keep words as object of painful distortion and evil intention.
verses.before: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are against me for evil.
verses.after: All day they twist my words; all their thoughts about me aim at harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are against me for evil.

verses.rationale: Follow read hide; bodily tracking and life threat explicit.
verses.before: They attack, they lurk, they watch my steps, as they wait for my life.
verses.after: They gather and hide, watching my footsteps, hoping to take my life.
verses.tsw_comparator: They attack, they lurk, they watch my steps, as they wait for my life.

verses.rationale: Difficult escape clause rendered rhetorical question; no added negative source text.
verses.before: Because of wickedness, cast them out; in anger bring down the peoples, O God.
verses.after: Will they escape despite their wrongdoing? God, bring the peoples down in anger!
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of wickedness, cast them out; in anger bring down the peoples, O God.

verses.rationale: Preserve counting, tears and skin-container image rather than generic remembering.
verses.before: You have kept count of my wanderings; put my tears in your bottle. Are they not in your book?
verses.after: You have counted my wanderings. Put my tears in your skin-bottle— are they not in your record?
verses.tsw_comparator: You have kept count of my wanderings; put my tears in your bottle. Are they not in your book?

verses.rationale: Keep day of calling and assurance not prediction of specific outcome date.
verses.before: Then my enemies will turn back on the day when I call. This I know, that God is for me.
verses.after: Then my enemies will turn back on the day I call. This I know: God is for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then my enemies will turn back on the day when I call. This I know, that God is for me.

verses.rationale: Repeat both parallel clauses and distinct divine designations.
verses.before: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
verses.after: In God I praise the word; in the LORD I praise the word.
verses.tsw_comparator: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,

verses.rationale: Preserve human noun different from flesh in earlier refrain.
verses.before: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can humans do to me?
verses.after: In God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can a human do to me?
verses.tsw_comparator: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can humans do to me?

verses.rationale: Explain upon me as obligation without losing sacrificial thanksgiving.
verses.before: O God, I must perform my vows to you; I will render thank offerings to you.
verses.after: God, my vows to you are binding on me; I will fulfill them with thank offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, I must perform my vows to you; I will render thank offerings to you.

verses.rationale: Render rhetorical have you not affirmatively; keep living light and walking purpose.
verses.before: For you have delivered my soul from death, indeed my feet from falling, so that I may walk before God in the light of life.
verses.after: You have rescued my life from death, and my feet from stumbling, so I may walk before God in the light of the living.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have delivered my soul from death, indeed my feet from falling, so that I may walk before God in the light of life.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated plea/refuge and all title elements without selecting a cave location.
verses.before: Be gracious to me, O God, be gracious to me, for in you my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge, until destruction passes by.
verses.after: For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul into the cave. Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me! I take refuge in you; in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge until destruction passes by.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be gracious to me, O God, be gracious to me, for in you my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge, until destruction passes by.

verses.rationale: Gomer completion left broad rather than inserting a detailed plan.
verses.before: I call to God Most High, to God who fulfills his purpose for me.
verses.after: I call to God Most High, to God who brings things to completion for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I call to God Most High, to God who fulfills his purpose for me.

verses.rationale: Keep two sending clauses; reproach clause could describe enemy, note.
verses.before: He will send from heaven and save me; he will put to shame people who trample on me. Selah God will send forth his steadfast love and his faithfulness.
verses.after: He will send from heaven and save me; he will put my pursuer to shame. Selah. God will send his faithful love and faithfulness.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will send from heaven and save me; he will put to shame those who trample on me. Selah God will send forth his steadfast love and his faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Preserve intertwined fire/lion/weapon imagery and human referent, devour contextual expansion.
verses.before: My soul is among lions; I lie down among people who breathe out fire— people whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
verses.after: My life is among lions; I lie down among those burning to devour— human beings whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul is in the midst of lions; I lie down among those who breathe out fire— people whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.

verses.rationale: Maintain exaltation petition and cosmic scope as refrain.
verses.before: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let your glory be over all the earth.
verses.after: Rise high above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let your glory be over all the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep dejection and reversal without moralizing addition.
verses.before: They set a net for my steps; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit in my path, but they have fallen into it themselves. Selah
verses.after: They set a net for my steps; I was bowed down. They dug a pit in front of me and fell into it themselves. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set a net for my steps; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit in my path, but they have fallen into it themselves. Selah

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic doubled heart and two musical verbs.
verses.before: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make melody.
verses.after: My heart is steady, God; my heart is steady. I will sing and make music.
verses.tsw_comparator: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make melody.

verses.rationale: Keep glory self-address and audacious dawn-waking image, not simply early rising.
verses.before: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awake the dawn.
verses.after: Wake up, my glory! Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awake the dawn.

verses.rationale: Preserve international parallel praise.
verses.before: I will thank you, Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to you among the nations.
verses.after: I will thank you among the peoples, Lord; I will make music to you among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will thank you, Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to you among the nations.

verses.rationale: Keep vertical paired qualities linked to verse 3.
verses.before: For your steadfast love is great to the heavens, and your faithfulness to the clouds.
verses.after: Your faithful love reaches high to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your steadfast love is great to the heavens, and your faithfulness to the clouds.

verses.rationale: Repeat verse 5 exactly to support audible structure.
verses.before: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let your glory be over all the earth.
verses.after: Rise high above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let your glory be over all the earth.

verses.rationale: Pinned elem silence difficult; preserve without silently repointing gods or rulers, note alternatives.
verses.before: Indeed, are you silent, you gods? Do you judge fairly, you children of humankind?
verses.after: For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam. Do you really speak justice, you silent ones? Do you judge people fairly?
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, are you silent, you gods? Do you judge fairly, you children of humankind?

verses.rationale: Judicial weighing image turned violent, heart and hands both retained.
verses.before: Even from the heart you work injustice; your hands weigh out violence on the earth.
verses.after: No! In your hearts you work injustice; on earth your hands weigh out violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even from the heart you work injustice; your hands weigh out violence on the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep hyperbolic birth accusation, not convert into doctrinal explanation.
verses.before: The wicked go astray from the womb; they are liars from birth.
verses.after: The wicked go astray from the womb; from birth, liars wander off.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked go astray from the womb; they are liars from birth.

verses.rationale: Keep ancient deaf-snake image even though biological description is not modern science.
verses.before: Their venom is like the venom of a snake; like a deaf adder that closes its ears,
verses.after: Their venom is like a snake’s venom, like a deaf cobra that stops its ears,
verses.tsw_comparator: Their venom is like the venom of a snake; like a deaf adder that closes its ears,

verses.rationale: Continue cobra image and charm expertise.
verses.before: unable to hear the sound of charmers, of a skilled enchanter.
verses.after: refusing to hear the voice of charmers, however skillfully they cast their spells.
verses.tsw_comparator: unable to hear the sound of charmers, of a skilled enchanter.

verses.rationale: Keep both violent commands and lion metaphor.
verses.before: O God, break the teeth in their mouths; tear out the fangs of the young lions, O Lord!
verses.after: God, smash the teeth in their mouths! LORD, break the young lions’ fangs!
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, break the teeth in their mouths; tear out the fangs of the young lions, O Lord!

verses.rationale: Follow read plural arrows, preserve singular subject shift and difficult cut-off image.
verses.before: Let them vanish like water that runs away; when he aims his arrows, let them be cut off.
verses.after: Let them dissolve like water flowing away. When he aims his arrows, let them be blunted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them vanish like water that runs away; when he aims his arrows, let them be cut off.

verses.rationale: Retain disturbing snail and stillbirth comparison without euphemism; note poetry not judgment on bereaved.
verses.before: Like a snail that melts as it moves, like a stillborn child who never sees the sun,
verses.after: Like a snail melting as it moves, like a woman’s stillborn child, let them never see the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a snail that melts as it moves, like a stillborn child who never sees the sun,

verses.rationale: Retain difficult pots/thorns/wind sequence; green/burning interpretive choice disclosed.
verses.before: before your pots can feel the heat of thorns— whether green or burning—he will sweep them away.
verses.after: Before your pots can feel the thorn-fire, whether green or burning, let him sweep it away.
verses.tsw_comparator: before your pots can feel the heat of thorns— whether green or burning—he will sweep them away.

verses.rationale: Preserve delight in vengeance and blood; use collective English for the generic righteous and wicked figures.
verses.before: The righteous will be glad when they look vengeance; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
verses.after: The righteous will rejoice to see vengeance; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous will be glad when they behold vengeance; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Keep fruit image and doubled indeed, plural participle construed with God.
verses.before: And people will say, "Surely there is a reward for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on earth."
verses.after: Then people will say, “There really is fruit for the righteous; there really is a God who judges on earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And people will say, "Surely there is a reward for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on earth."

verses.rationale: Title watch and murder threat explicit; sagab height retained.
verses.before: Deliver me from my enemies, my God; protect me from people who rise against me.
verses.after: For the music leader. “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, when Saul sent men to watch the house and kill him. Rescue me from my enemies, my God; set me high beyond those rising against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver me from my enemies, my God; protect me from those who rise against me.

verses.rationale: Keep two requests and specific violent men.
verses.before: Deliver me from workers of wickedness, and save me from men of blood.
verses.after: Rescue me from evildoers; save me from men of bloodshed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver me from workers of wickedness, and save me from men of blood.

verses.rationale: Preserve claimed innocence in this conflict, not universal sinlessness.
verses.before: For, look, they lie in wait for my soul; the mighty gather against me, not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O LORD.
verses.after: Look! They lie in wait for my life; fierce men gather against me— not because I rebelled or sinned, LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: For, behold, they lie in wait for my soul; the mighty gather against me, not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain military preparations and bold wake demand.
verses.before: Without fault they run and prepare themselves. Rouse yourself to help me, and see!
verses.after: Though I have done no wrong, they run and take their positions. Wake up! Come to meet me and see!
verses.tsw_comparator: Without fault they run and prepare themselves. Rouse yourself to help me, and see!

verses.rationale: Keep scope widening from local attackers to nations and refusal of mercy.
verses.before: You, LORD God of Hosts, God of Israel, arise to punish all the nations. Do not be merciful to all treacherous workers of evil. Selah.
verses.after: You, LORD God of Armies, God of Israel, wake up to call all the nations to account! Show no favor to any treacherous evildoer. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: You, LORD God of Hosts, God of Israel, arise to punish all the nations. Do not be merciful to all treacherous workers of evil. Selah.

verses.rationale: Dog patrol image and evening refrain.
verses.before: They return at evening; they growl like a dog, and go around the city.
verses.after: They return at evening, growling like dogs, and circle the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: They return at evening; they growl like a dog, and go around the city.

verses.rationale: Preserve spewing and sword speech, quoted challenge implicit context supplied us.
verses.before: Look, they spew with their mouths; swords are on their lips, for who hears?
verses.after: Listen to what pours from their mouths! Swords are on their lips: “Who can hear us?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, they spew with their mouths; swords are on their lips, for who hears?

verses.rationale: Maintain divine ridicule without softened disapproval.
verses.before: But you, LORD, laugh at them; you mock all the nations.
verses.after: But you, LORD, laugh at them; you mock all the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, LORD, laugh at them; you mock all the nations.

verses.rationale: Keep pinned his strength rather than harmonizing to my strength in verse 17; note ellipsis.
verses.before: O, my strength, I will wait for you; for God is my fortress.
verses.after: Against his strength, I watch for you, for God is my stronghold.
verses.tsw_comparator: O, my strength, I will wait for you; for God is my fortress.

verses.rationale: Follow read my love; no added delight or triumph in look upon.
verses.before: My God of steadfast love will come to meet me; God will let me look upon my enemies.
verses.after: My God of faithful love will come to meet me; God will let me look upon those watching for my fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: My God of steadfast love will come to meet me; God will let me look upon my enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserve do not kill despite subsequent consume; no smoothing tension.
verses.before: Do not kill them, lest my people forget; make them wander by your power and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
verses.after: Do not kill them, or my people may forget. Make them wander by your might; bring them low, Lord, our shield.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not kill them, lest my people forget; make them wander by your power and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.

verses.rationale: Keep speech, pride and requested entrapment.
verses.before: By the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride, for the curses and lies they utter.
verses.after: For the sin of their mouths, the words on their lips, let them be caught in their pride, for the curses and lies they speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride, for the curses and lies they utter.

verses.rationale: Keep doubled consume and shifting they without specifying survivors.
verses.before: Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more. Then it will be known that God rules over Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah.
verses.after: Consume them in wrath; consume them until they are gone! Then they will know that God rules over Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more. Then it will be known that God rules over Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah.

verses.rationale: Repeat verse 6 with the same wording.
verses.before: At evening let them return; let them howl like a dog, and go around the city.
verses.after: They return at evening, growling like dogs, and circle the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: At evening let them return; let them howl like a dog, and go around the city.

verses.rationale: Pinned lodging verb retained rather than alternate growling; note ambiguity.
verses.before: They wander for food; if they are not satisfied, they remain all night.
verses.after: They wander in search of food; if they are not satisfied, they stay the night.
verses.tsw_comparator: They wander for food; if they are not satisfied, they remain all night.

verses.rationale: Contrast morning singer with evening dogs; two refuge images.
verses.before: Yet I will sing of your strength; in the morning I will sing of your steadfast love. For you have been my fortress, and a refuge in the day of my distress.
verses.after: But I will sing of your strength; at morning I will sing aloud of your faithful love. You have been my stronghold, a place to flee on my day of distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will sing of your strength; in the morning I will sing of your steadfast love. For you have been my fortress, and a refuge in the day of my distress.

verses.rationale: Keep my strength distinct from verse 9 and repeated stronghold/love.
verses.before: O my strength, I will sing praises to you, for God is my fortress, the God of steadfast love.
verses.after: My strength, I will make music to you, for God is my stronghold, my God of faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: O my strength, I will sing praises to you, for God is my fortress, the God of steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Bind both title records and opening; preserve all names, Joab, twelve thousand and divine agency without harmonizing Samuel.
verses.before: O God, you have rejected us, broken through us; you were angry—restore us.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to “The Lily of Testimony.” A miktam of David. For teaching. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. God, you have rejected us and broken through our defenses. You have been angry; restore us!
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, you have rejected us, broken through us; you were angry—restore us.

verses.rationale: Earthquake and healing imagery retain national catastrophe.
verses.before: You have made the earth tremble; you have split it open. Heal its fractures, for it is shaking.
verses.after: You have shaken the land and split it open. Heal its fractures, for it is tottering.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have made the earth tremble; you have split it open. Heal its fractures, for it is shaking.

verses.rationale: Keep God as giver of distress and intoxicating wine image.
verses.before: You have shown your people harsh things; you have given us wine to drink that makes us stagger.
verses.after: You have made your people see hardship; you have given us wine that sends us staggering.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have shown your people harsh things; you have given us wine to drink that makes us stagger.

verses.rationale: Pinned qoshet truth chosen; alternate flee before bow requires note.
verses.before: You have set up a banner for people who fear you, to be lifted up because of truth. Selah.
verses.after: You have given those who fear you a banner to raise for the sake of truth. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have set up a banner for those who fear you, to be lifted up because of truth. Selah.

verses.rationale: Follow read me versus written us, retain communal beloved and right hand.
verses.before: That your beloved ones may be delivered, save with your right hand, and answer us.
verses.after: So that those you love may be rescued, save with your right hand and answer me.
verses.tsw_comparator: That your beloved ones may be delivered, save with your right hand, and answer us.

verses.rationale: Open divine speech and retain land allocation, holiness/sanctuary ambiguity noted.
verses.before: God has spoken in his holiness: "I will exult, I will divide Shechem, and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
verses.after: God has spoken in his holiness: “I will rejoice! I will divide Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
verses.tsw_comparator: God has spoken in his holiness: "I will exult, I will divide Shechem, and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

verses.rationale: Preserve four tribal/territorial names and head/staff authority images.
verses.before: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is my helmet, Judah my scepter.
verses.after: Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is my head’s protection, Judah is my ruling staff.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is my helmet, Judah my scepter.

verses.rationale: Pinned imperative over me retained despite difficult triumphant sense; do not harmonize Psalm 108.
verses.before: Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I throw my shoe; over Philistia I shout in triumph."
verses.after: Moab is my washbasin; on Edom I throw my sandal. Philistia, shout over me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I throw my shoe; over Philistia I shout in triumph."

verses.rationale: Close oracle before questions; unidentified fortified city stays unnamed.
verses.before: Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
verses.after: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me as far as Edom?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?

verses.rationale: Preserve rejected lament and absence, not force a confident answer.
verses.before: Have you not, O God, cast us off? And you do not go out with our armies, O God?
verses.after: Is it not you, God, who rejected us? God, you do not march out with our armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you not, O God, cast us off? And you do not go out with our armies, O God?

verses.rationale: Human help contrast not abstract contempt for people.
verses.before: Grant us help against the foe, for human deliverance is worthless.
verses.after: Give us help against the foe; human rescue is empty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grant us help against the foe, for human deliverance is worthless.

verses.rationale: Keep martial conclusion and divine trampling.
verses.before: In God we will do valiantly; it is he who will tread down our foes.
verses.after: With God we will act with strength; he will trample our foes.
verses.tsw_comparator: In God we shall do valiantly; it is he who will tread down our foes.

verses.rationale: Title singular instrument retained and two appeals.
verses.before: Hear, O God, my cry; pay attention to my prayer.
verses.after: For the music leader. With a stringed instrument. Of David. Hear my cry, God; pay attention to my prayer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, O God, my cry; pay attention to my prayer.

verses.rationale: Retain the height comparison as high above me without making inability to reach it an explicit source claim.
verses.before: From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart grows faint; lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
verses.after: From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart grows faint. Lead me to the rock high above me.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart grows faint; lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

verses.rationale: Keep refuge and tower images distinct.
verses.before: For you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower against the enemy.
verses.after: You have been a refuge for me, a strong tower against the enemy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower against the enemy.

verses.rationale: Maintain tent guest and bird shelter together.
verses.before: Let me dwell in your tent forever; let me find refuge under the cover of your wings. Selah.
verses.after: Let me stay in your tent forever; let me take refuge under the shelter of your wings. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let me dwell in your tent forever; let me find refuge under the cover of your wings. Selah.

verses.rationale: Supply recipient me from speaker, preserve inheritance and name.
verses.before: For you, O God, have heard my vows; you have given the heritage of people who fear your name.
verses.after: You, God, have heard my vows; you have given me the inheritance of those who fear your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you, O God, have heard my vows; you have given the heritage of those who fear your name.

verses.rationale: Keep royal longevity prayer and repeated days.
verses.before: Prolong the days of the king; may his years be as many generations.
verses.after: Add days to the king’s days; let his years stretch through generation after generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Prolong the days of the king; may his years be as many generations.

verses.rationale: Keep third-person king and personified guards without naming dynasty.
verses.before: May he sit enthroned before God forever; appoint steadfast love and faithfulness to guard him.
verses.after: May he sit before God forever; appoint faithful love and faithfulness to guard him.
verses.tsw_comparator: May he sit enthroned before God forever; appoint steadfast love and faithfulness to guard him.

verses.rationale: Return to first person and vows, preserve day by day.
verses.before: So I will sing praise to your name forever, to fulfill my vows day after day.
verses.after: Then I will always make music to your name, fulfilling my vows day by day.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will sing praise to your name forever, to fulfill my vows day after day.

verses.rationale: Title preserved; silence and exclusive focus carried in first refrain.
verses.before: Only in God is my soul at rest; from him is my salvation.
verses.after: For the music leader. According to Jeduthun. A psalm of David. For God alone I wait in silence; my rescue comes from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only in God is my soul at rest; from him is my salvation.

verses.rationale: Keep greatly, absent in later refrain, to preserve progression.
verses.before: Only he is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I will not be greatly shaken.
verses.after: He alone is my rock and my rescue, my stronghold; I will not be greatly shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only he is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be greatly shaken.

verses.rationale: Keep vulnerable singular against collective attackers; difficult murder verb active per pinned pointing.
verses.before: How long will all of you attack a man to batter him, a leaning wall, a tottering fence?
verses.after: How long will you all attack one man, trying to murder him as though he were a leaning wall, a fence about to fall?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long will all of you attack a man to batter him, a leaning wall, a tottering fence?

verses.rationale: Preserve social elevation and outer/inner contrast, normalize singular mouth to plural people.
verses.before: Only from his exaltation they have counseled to thrust him down; they delight in falsehood. With their mouth they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah
verses.after: They plot only to topple him from his high place. They delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only from his exaltation they have counseled to thrust him down; they delight in falsehood. With their mouth they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah

verses.rationale: Self-command rather than identical statement, hope versus rescue.
verses.before: Only in God, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him.
verses.after: Wait in silence for God alone, my soul; my hope comes from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only in God, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him.

verses.rationale: Repeat refrain without greatly, retain real difference from verse 2.
verses.before: Only he is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I will not be shaken.
verses.after: He alone is my rock and my rescue, my stronghold; I will not be shaken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only he is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be shaken.

verses.rationale: Keep honor and doubled God reference, unusual in construction not erased.
verses.before: On God rests my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is God.
verses.after: My rescue and my honor rest on God; my mighty rock, my refuge, is in God.
verses.tsw_comparator: On God rests my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is God.

verses.rationale: Shift from self-address to community and pouring heart image.
verses.before: Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us. Selah
verses.after: Trust him at all times, you people; pour out your hearts before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us. Selah

verses.rationale: Social distinction beney adam/ish contextual; all together inadequate, not class contempt.
verses.before: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie; in the balances they go up; together they are lighter than a breath.
verses.after: Ordinary people are a breath; the powerful are a lie. Put them together on the scales and they rise— lighter than a breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie; in the balances they go up; together they are lighter than a breath.

verses.rationale: Preserve oppression/robbery distinct from ordinary growing wealth.
verses.before: Trust not in oppression, and do not put vain hope in robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
verses.after: Do not trust in extortion or put empty hopes in stolen goods. If wealth increases, do not set your heart on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Trust not in oppression, and do not put vain hope in robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.

verses.rationale: Keep numeric saying and clause continuing into faithful love.
verses.before: One thing God has spoken, two things I have heard: that power belongs to God,
verses.after: God has spoken once; twice I have heard this: strength belongs to God,
verses.tsw_comparator: One thing God has spoken, two things I have heard: that power belongs to God,

verses.rationale: Direct-address shift and deeds-based repayment without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: and to you, O Lord, belongs steadfast love, for you will repay everyone according to their work.
verses.after: and faithful love belongs to you, Lord. You repay each person according to what they do.
verses.tsw_comparator: and to you, O Lord, belongs steadfast love, for you will repay everyone according to their work.

verses.rationale: Title Judah preserved; physical flesh and thirst alongside whole being, seek eagerly rather than mandatory dawn.
verses.before: O God, you are my God; I earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you, in a dry and weary land without water.
verses.after: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. God, you are my God; I seek you eagerly. My whole being thirsts for you; my flesh longs for you in a dry, weary land with no water.
verses.tsw_comparator: O God, you are my God; I earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you, in a dry and weary land without water.

verses.rationale: Keep past sanctuary sight rather than turning into future wish.
verses.before: Thus I have beheld you in the sanctuary, seeing your power and your glory.
verses.after: So I have gazed on you in the sanctuary, seeing your strength and glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus I have beheld you in the sanctuary, seeing your power and your glory.

verses.rationale: Retain startling comparison not soften to enriching life.
verses.before: Because your steadfast love is better than life, my lips will praise you.
verses.after: Your faithful love is better than life; my lips will praise you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because your steadfast love is better than life, my lips will praise you.

verses.rationale: Life and embodied prayer with name retained.
verses.before: So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift up my hands.
verses.after: So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift my hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift up my hands.

verses.rationale: Keep ancient fat richness image rather than generic satisfaction.
verses.before: My soul will be satisfied as with the richest of foods, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips
verses.after: I will be satisfied as with fat and rich food; my mouth will praise you with joyful lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul will be satisfied as with the richest of foods, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips

verses.rationale: Sleep setting and night divisions preserved.
verses.before: when I remember you upon my bed, and meditate on you in the night watches.
verses.after: When I remember you on my bed, I ponder you through the night watches.
verses.tsw_comparator: when I remember you upon my bed, and meditate on you in the night watches.

verses.rationale: Wings recur as shelter and joy.
verses.before: For you have been my help, and in the shadow of your wings I will sing for joy.
verses.after: You have been my help; in the shadow of your wings I sing aloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have been my help, and in the shadow of your wings I will sing for joy.

verses.rationale: Mutual holding and specific right hand retained.
verses.before: My soul clings to you; your right hand upholds me.
verses.after: My whole being clings to you; your right hand holds me fast.
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul clings to you; your right hand upholds me.

verses.rationale: Contrast enemy life-seeking with descent, not assert a developed hell doctrine.
verses.before: But people who seek to destroy my life will go down into the depths of the earth;
verses.after: But those who seek to destroy my life will go into the depths of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: But those who seek to destroy my life shall go down into the depths of the earth;

verses.rationale: Keep death and scavenger image, jackals rather than domesticated fox stereotype.
verses.before: they will be given over to the power of the sword; they will be the portion of jackals.
verses.after: They will be handed over to the sword and become a portion for jackals.
verses.tsw_comparator: they shall be given over to the power of the sword; they shall be the portion of jackals.

verses.rationale: Leave him God/king ambiguity in note, royal third person not replaced by I.
verses.before: But the king will rejoice in God; everyone who swear by him will exult, for the mouths of liars will be stopped.
verses.after: But the king will rejoice in God; everyone who swears by him will glory, for the mouths that speak lies will be stopped.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the king shall rejoice in God; all who swear by him shall exult, for the mouths of liars shall be stopped.

verses.rationale: Preserve complaint and fear caused by enemy, title bound with opening.
verses.before: Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint; preserve my life from the terror of the enemy.
verses.after: For the music leader. A psalm of David. God, hear my voice as I complain; protect my life from the enemy’s terror.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint; preserve my life from the terror of the enemy.

verses.rationale: Quiet conspiracy and noisy gathering contrast.
verses.before: Hide me from the secret counsel of evildoers, from the tumult of workers of iniquity,
verses.after: Hide me from the secret counsel of evildoers, from the tumult of those who do harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hide me from the secret counsel of evildoers, from the tumult of workers of iniquity,

verses.rationale: Keep speech weapons and line running into purpose.
verses.before: who sharpen their tongue like a sword and aim their arrows—bitter words
verses.after: They sharpen their tongues like swords and aim bitter words like arrows,
verses.tsw_comparator: who sharpen their tongue like a sword and aim their arrows—bitter words

verses.rationale: Suddenly and fear prepare divine reversal, singular target retained.
verses.before: to shoot in secret at the blameless; suddenly they shoot at him and do not fear.
verses.after: to shoot at the blameless from hiding. They shoot him suddenly, without fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: to shoot in secret at the blameless; suddenly they shoot at him and do not fear.

verses.rationale: Keep mutual encouragement and concealed trap challenge, pronoun ambiguity noted.
verses.before: They hold fast to their evil purpose; they talk of laying snares secretly; they say, “Who will see them?”
verses.after: They encourage each other in an evil plan; they talk of hiding snares, saying, “Who will see them?”
verses.tsw_comparator: They hold fast to their evil purpose; they talk of laying snares secretly; they say, “Who will see them?”

verses.rationale: Difficult searching wordplay and quoted first-plural preserved; note alternatives.
verses.before: They devise injustices, saying, “We have perfected a secret plan.” Both the inner thought and the heart of a person are deep.
verses.after: They search out ways to do wrong: “We have perfected a thoroughly searched-out plan!” A person’s inward thought and heart are deep.
verses.tsw_comparator: They devise injustices, saying, “We have perfected a secret plan.” Both the inner thought and the heart of a person are deep.

verses.rationale: Keep enemy weapons and suddenly turned back on them.
verses.before: Yet God will shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly they will be wounded.
verses.after: But God shoots them with an arrow; suddenly they are wounded.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God will shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly they will be wounded.

verses.rationale: Difficult mixed-number syntax rendered own-tongue recoil; gestures versus flight note.
verses.before: They will be made to stumble, their own tongue against them; everyone who see them will shake their heads.
verses.after: Their own tongues bring them down; everyone who sees them shakes their head.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be made to stumble, their own tongue against them; all who see them will shake their heads.

verses.rationale: Human fear reverses attackers fearlessness; recount and understand both.
verses.before: Then all people will fear; they will declare the work of God, and will consider what He has done.
verses.after: Then all people will fear; they will tell what God has done and ponder his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all people will fear; they will declare the work of God, and will consider what He has done.

verses.rationale: Close with public rejoicing, refuge and heart answering hidden wicked hearts.
verses.before: The righteous will rejoice in LORD and take refuge in him; all the upright in heart will glory.
verses.after: Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in him; let all the upright in heart glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: The righteous will rejoice in LORD and take refuge in him; all the upright in heart will glory.

comparative_references.scope: All 609 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording is retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
